newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 18.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Friday.
- Irish police are to step up surveillance at ports to stem the flow of illegal immigrants amid suspicions that organised groups are smuggling in refugees in return for large fees.
- The Chinese government has postponed a visit to Ireland in May in protest at Ireland's support for a Danish UN resolution criticising China's human rights record.
- Ireland's current economic boom is set to continue into 1999, says a report to be published today by Finance Minister Ruiairi Quinn.

- Average salaries paid to executive directors at Irish Life rose by 17 percent last year and other payments by 21 percent, with the top four directors sharing 1.05 million Irish pounds. - The Irish blood transfusion service has reversed an earlier position and admitted legal liability in all cases of hepatitis C caused by contaminated blood products.
- Former prime minister Charles Haughey is to be named by Irish department store millionaire Ben Dunne as the politician at the centre of a 1.1 million Irish pound payout.

- Jefferson Smurfit Corporation, the U.S. associate of the Irish group, has turned in net losses of 7 million dollars for the first quarter of 1997 compared with a net profit of 53 million dollars in the same period in 1996, a loss the company blames on weak product prices.
- Most Irish companies are unprepared for the true cost of solving the Year 2000 computer problem, accounting firm Deloitte & Touche has warned.
- New national radio station Radio Ireland has made a 1 million Irish pound bid to lure talk show star Gerry Ryan away from national broadcasting network RTE.
- Suppliers to food company Waterford are 'hostile' to a 2.5 billion pound merger proposal from Avonmore - a critical board meeting is due to take place today.
- French oil group Total plans to spend 15 million Irish pounds exploring for oil and gas 100 miles off the coast of Kerry.
